bull_bear.body: Rights issue ₹260cr allocated: ₹55cr debt repayment, ₹107cr promoter loan conversion, ₹85cr Tritium support, ₹12cr corporate purposes; IPO funds prioritized for Hyderabad plant (₹292cr), working capital, and R&D; no dividend or buyback planned
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Tritium turnaround slower than expected; geopolitical supply chain delays for rare earth components (minor impact); EV price wars compressing margins; project execution delays due to monsoon/approvals; consolidation risk from smaller competitors
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and transparent; acknowledged Q1 miss but emphasized strong order book and pipeline; highlighted operational discipline, product innovation, and long-term strategic bets; tone focused on execution and FY26 guidance adherence
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Exicom is the only Indian EV charger maker designing its own controller (CPU) in-house — a deep tech differentiator; Tritium's lifetime warranty on power modules is a global first, signaling confidence in reliability and a potential industry standard setter
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Net Debt : 370.1 Cr at consolidated level" is the only balance-sheet headline given; no dividend or buyback is mentioned anywhere in the deck.
- IPO proceeds are exhausted: other income was lower "on account of FD interest of IPO funds which have now been completely utilised."
- Capital has gone into inorganic expansion and capacity — 2024 saw "Successful IPO. Listed on NSE and BSE. Tritium Acquisition", followed by the 2026 Hyderabad plant.
- Consolidated segment assets are skewed to EV Charger at 1,110.2 Rs Cr versus Critical Power at 781.4 Rs Cr as of June 30, 2026, against EV Charger segment liabilities of 802.5 Rs Cr.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Critical Power: ₹98cr revenue (standalone), down due to Bharat Net/delays; 70% market share in rural telecom battery upgrades; 30% revenue from Africa/SE Asia; EV Chargers: ₹53cr standalone (61% QoQ growth), 50% AC/50% DC mix; Harmony Gen 2 adopted by 6 of top 10 customers; Tritium: $8M Q1 bookings, TRI-FLEX pipeline building, lifetime warranty on power modules launched
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tritium's prolonged losses and delayed turnaround | Servotech Power Systems | loser | Low | Servotech's growth is in solar/EPC; Exicom's scale, global reach, and integrated manufacturing give it structural advantage in pure-play EV charging |
| Lack of domestic manufacturing scale in EV charging | OEMs (Tata, Mahindra, Hyundai) | beneficiary | High | Exicom's Hyderabad plant and Gen 2 product will become preferred supplier for premium EV makers seeking reliable, high-margin charging infrastructure |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as a "Leading player for Energy Storage Systems & Power Management Systems" with a strong customer base including telecom and data centers, and projects deployed across India, Malaysia, Singapore, South Africa, Nigeria, etc.
- In Electric Mobility it claims to be "India's one of the Top EV charger company", with customers among major CPOs, OEMs and fleets and a product range spanning 3.3 kW to 600 kW output including distributed and BESS solutions.
- Critical Power strategy is framed around "Five forces redefining how operators buy site power": higher-density 5G loads, lead-acid to intelligent lithium, generator to hybrid energy, backup to active energy asset, and alarms to fleet intelligence.
- Positions on lifetime outcomes rather than price: "Operators increasingly evaluate site power through lifetime outcomes and Exicom's end to end product stack allows for low risk adjusted lifetime cost per network hour"; in Govt supplies the deck claims "Exicom has 60% market share of this project".
- Tritium is positioned around strategic customers: TRI-FLEX/DCFlex under field and lab validation by "one of the largest open public charging network and fleet company in the US", and the first GRID-FLEX system delivered to a hyperscale customer and operating since June.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Tritium] The overseas fast-charging arm remains loss-making at the consolidated level but shows momentum — Q1 bookings of USD 20.8m, described by the CEO as "~2x QoQ", with a stated "second consecutive quarter ~10Mn$ sales".
- [Regulation - Haryana] Building code notified 5-Jun-26 mandates 1:3 charge points per car park for commercial buildings and 1:5 for group housing/RWA, with 100% EV-ready conduits, basement and stilt charging allowed and EV infrastructure exempt from FAR.
- [Regulation - Delhi] Delhi EV Policy 2026 notified 30-Jun-26 with a ₹15,000 Cr four-year outlay, 30,000+ charging points planned, one charging station per OEM dealer, e-3W and e-N1 only from Jan-27, and e-2W subsidy up to ₹30,000.
- [Regulation - PM E-Drive] ₹504 Cr sanctioned in this tranche (~25% of the ₹2,000 Cr charging pool) for 4,874 public chargers, Karnataka largest at 1,243; the deck's own read is that this is "a positive for Industry. Not a very high target market for Exicom".
- [Plant transition] Manufacturing is mid-shift from Gurgaon to Hyderabad, with both plants running in parallel during the transition.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin improved to 32.7% (standalone) due to richer EV product mix and cost optimization; Harmony Gen 2 delivered higher value with margin expansion; Tritium's high fixed costs drag consolidated margins; Hyderabad plant to reduce per-unit cost by 15-20% at full capacity
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: 50% YoY standalone; EBITDA: 2.5x improvement; Order inflow: Sustained by ₹1,500cr backlog; Capex/commissioning: Hyderabad plant SOP in Oct 2025, full ramp-up by Q4FY26
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: ₹1,500+ crores total (₹1,200+ crores hardware), including large lithium-ion battery upgrades, Middle East/Africa exports, and EV charger framework agreements in Southeast Asia
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Global EV charging framework with Southeast Asia clean energy player; entry into electric trucking segment; DC microgrid-integrated charging solutions under development; potential Tritium product localization in India
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Q1 revenue missed due to project delays in Bharat Net and battery upgrades, but order book surged to ₹1,500+ crores with EV charging momentum accelerating; Hyderabad plant commissioning in Oct 2025 will unlock scale and margin expansion, while Tritium's TRI-FLEX and lifetime warranty signal long-term global potential.
